summary.headline: GPT Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue fell 9% to INR282 crores on West Bengal labour disruption, while consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 15.7% on Alcon signalling.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue declined 9% YoY to INR282 crores due to labour unavailability in West Bengal during April-May elections, which management says has since normalised. Consolidated revenue fell 3.4% to INR302 crores, but consolidated EBITDA rose 28.4% to INR47.5 crores (15.7% margin), helped by the Alcon signalling business and African operations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 30% and raised its FY27 EBITDA margin expectation to 14-15%, with 13-14% as the long-term range. Order book stood at INR4,303 crores and Q1 order inflow was only about INR130 crores against a INR3,000 crore annual target.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR283 crores in Q1, driven by railway bridges and road projects (NHAI Ganga Bridge Prayagraj, Rupnarayan Bridge Kolaghat, Kona Expressway).

segments.name: Sleeper
segments.commentary: INR19 crores revenue in Q1, supported by domestic demand, export orders from India to Bangladesh and international operations; management cites 14-15% sleeper margin.

segments.name: Alcon (signalling)
segments.commentary: Acquired Q4 FY26; contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and management guides INR100-120 crores for FY27, implying roughly INR70-80 crores incremental YoY per management.

segments.name: Power EPC (new)
segments.commentary: Entered with a ~INR53 crore contract from Power Grid Corporation of India for a Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh project; targets INR150-200 crores annual revenue in the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of approximately 30%, implying about INR1,700 crores total and roughly INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 (about INR150 crores per month).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 14-15%, 100-150 bps above the 13-14% long-term range, attributed to Alcon integration and better African operations.
FY27 order inflow target of INR3,000 crores; management said it expects to exceed this, as in FY26 (target INR2,000 crores, achieved INR2,400 crores).
Debt expected to reduce over FY27 with no net addition; debt-to-equity to move toward about 0.5x, partly funded by Alcon cash after merger.
Alcon to be merged into GPT Infra in ensuing quarters; African business expected to deliver strong inflows and a sizable South African order this quarter.
capex_capacity: Management did not discuss capex or new capacity additions on the call.
Alcon merger into GPT Infra expected in ensuing quarters, enabling bids for larger value contracts (INR1,500-2,000 crore EPC, 3-4 year execution).
Monsoon season in Q2 expected to affect execution pace.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,303 crores as of date, down from INR4,480 crores; Q1 fresh inflow about INR130 crores.
Signalling bids of over INR500 crores submitted; under technical evaluation, none converted to orders yet. Company is not L1 in any contract currently.
Addressable market: Indian Railways outlay of about INR1 trillion over six years for signalling (Kavach, electronic interlocking, DDEI); ~USD1.5 billion market cited.
West Bengal: INR895 crores railway investments approved centrally and INR2,100 crores state connectivity projects announced, including Bhagirathi Bridge and Chingrighata-New Town Corridor.
Africa: concrete sleeper business in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana; new South African order expected in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 30% FY27 growth given Q1 was flat, and can 9M growth reach 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was planned as flattish; the INR4,300 crore order book and some late-FY26 orders, with revenue from H2, support about INR1,400 crores over the balance nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins stay at the long-term 13-14% after 15.7% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin at 14-15%, with long-term range unchanged at 13-14%; standalone Q1 margin was about 13.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Contract assets and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract assets were about INR430 crores at March end, up about 5%; around INR200 crores has since been billed and received. Q1 operating cash flow not disclosed; to be given in the September quarter or half-year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt position and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt has not risen materially versus March; management expects to reduce debt over FY27 and targets debt-to-equity near 0.5x from about 0.65x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q1 standalone execution slip and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour availability was affected for about half the quarter (April-May); workforce normalised from May, and management expects a monthly run rate of about INR150 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Alcon revenue contribution and signalling bid status?
qa_highlights.answer: Alcon contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and is guided at INR100-120 crores for FY27; signalling bids worth over INR500 crores are under technical evaluation.

risks_watch: Execution ramp: FY27 30% growth needs about INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 versus INR282 crores standalone in Q1; monsoon season in Q2 adds risk.
Order inflow: Q1 inflow of about INR130 crores against INR3,000 crore annual target; order book fell from INR4,480 crores to INR4,300 crores.
Working capital: contract assets elevated, cash flow from operations weak in recent years; Q1 CFO not disclosed.
Alcon merger timing and integration, and conversion of over INR500 crores of signalling bids.
Power EPC: prior execution challenges in this segment; the new entry is small (INR53 crores) and margin target of 13-14% is unproven.
Subcontracting cost ratio moved from about 30% highs to about 20%; management says it depends on project cycle.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year guidance and margins, but evasive on specifics: declined to give Q1 operating cash flow, L1 status, and signalling share of railway bids. Q1 shortfall was attributed to a transient labour issue.
